purpose: Teach: 北方/ケネディ/都立/近鉄/東急/Ｊリーグ/エンジニアリング/デスノート

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが北方領土返還運動に参加された
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father was involved in the Northern Territories return movement.
lines.style: Gentle, reflective opening. Soft voice, almost testing whether she remembers. Paced like he's offering a memory to her, not stating fact. Slight pause after 'Gran' — the name carries weight and time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ケネディ大統領の暗殺に絶句されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — your grandfather, he was quite struck when President Kennedy was assassinated, wasn't he?
lines.style: Warm, conversational, slightly teasing. She's not answering his question directly; she's offering her own memory back. A smile in her voice. The 'dear' lands lightly — affectionate, not condescending.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが都立高校で教鞭をとられた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father was teaching at Toritsu High School.
lines.style: Same reflective register as before. He's gently weaving the details of the past. Quiet certainty — he's checking these facts with her, but he remembers them clearly. Even pacing, allowing space between phrases.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、近鉄沿線にお住まいだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, he lived along the Kintetsu line, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Playful redirect. She's doing it again — offering her own detail instead of confirming his. Light, knowing tone. The question carries gentle humor — she's teasing him a little, keeping him present with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが東急百貨店で買い物された
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father used to shop at Tokyu Department Store.
lines.style: The same patient, almost ceremonial tone. He's unhurried. These small details matter to him — where people shopped, what they wore, how they moved through the city. Delivered with quiet reverence for the ordinary.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、Ｊリーグ発足の年を覚えてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, he remembered what year the J-League started, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, slightly mischievous. She's keeping the conversation alive by adding her own layer. Delivered with gentle amusement — she knows he's lost in memories and she's lovingly nudging him. The question is almost rhetorical, delivered with affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがエンジニアリング会社にお勤めだった
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father worked for an engineering company.
lines.style: Quiet, steady. The rhythm is becoming almost meditative now — line by line, memory by memory. His voice is calm and grounded. There's acceptance in how he delivers this, like he's piecing together a life he once knew.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様がデスノートを読まれて驚いてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, he was quite surprised when your grandchild read Death Note, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, close, with gentle humor at the end. She's found something playful in the memories — the generations, the surprise of modern things. Delivered softly, almost in his ear. The 'dear' here is tender, not teasing.
